CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#763488: Memory corruption vulnerabilities in PHP
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Two memory-related vulnerabilities have been identified in PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. An unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to PHP web services can exploit these vulnerabilities via specially crafted HTTP requests to potentially achieve arbitrary code execution.

Description

PHP is a widely used open-source scripting language designed for web development and server-side applications. It powers millions of websites and web applications worldwide and can be deployed through a variety of server configurations, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed.

CVE-2026-109618: A memory corruption vulnerability exists in the out-of-memory (OOM) handling mechanism of PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. The vulnerability occurs when an OOM condition interrupts request processing while internal request data is only partially initialized; subsequent cleanup routines may access the invalid memory, potentially causing memory corruption and enabling arbitrary code execution.

CVE-2026-109619: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the global state management of PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. The vulnerability occurs when a worker retains a reference to request-owned state after its backing memory has been freed. A subsequent request handled by the same worker can access this stale state before normal request initialization resets it, potentially causing memory corruption and enabling arbitrary code execution.

Impact

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities allows an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP requests, compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the web service and underlying infrastructure. Apache mod_php deployments are at particularly high risk, as proof-of-concept exploitation has demonstrated that unauthenticated requests can trigger the attack before any application code executes.

Solution

Refer to the Vendor Information section below for newly patched versions of PHP that remediate these vulnerabilities. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12. Source downloads are available on the official PHP release page at php.net/downloads.

Linux users are advised to check with their distribution vendor for updated packages, as many distributions received patches in advance. For PHP 8.1 and older versions that no longer receive official updates from the PHP project, contact your LTS vendor for backported fixes or upgrade to a supported version. The PHP security team has provided limited source backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 to assist users building from source or without access to an LTS vendor.

If immediate patching is not feasible, the following temporary mitigation measures may reduce exposure to specific attack paths, though they do not provide complete protection. Because these vulnerabilities are closely related, mitigations for both CVEs should be applied:

For CVE-2026-109618 (OOM Corruption):

  • Set memory_limit=-1 at an administrative level so it cannot be overridden by applications, for example via php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration.
  • Set a low post_max_size (8M for applications without file uploads, 32M if uploads are necessary).
  • Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size.
  • Enforce limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request-body size, input variable count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth.
  • Use container or cgroup limits as an availability boundary with policies that kill only the affected worker. Notably, RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA should not be used to bound memory, as these cause mmap() to fail once the limit is reached, triggering the vulnerable code path rather than preventing it.

For CVE-2026-109619 (Stale Global State):

  • Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini, FPM pool, or server configuration and restart all workers.
  • On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart all workers.
  • Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization.
  • Remediate attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts.

System owners can limit the potential impact of successful exploitation by implementing network segmentation and ensuring that PHP installations are configured to run with minimum necessary privileges. Users are advised to monitor closely for unusual PHP process behavior or unexpected memory allocation patterns.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to OpenAI, Wiz, and Ryan at Calif.io for reporting these vulnerabilities. This document was written by Molly Jaconski.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#645818: Xerj Console API Authentication Bypass Leads to Unauthorized Credential Minting
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

An authentication bypass vulnerability in the Xerj Console API allows sessions to bypass passkey-backed requirements during token issuance. By exploiting this flaw, an attacker with an existing valid token can create independent, persistent successor credentials directly through the console API. This allows the attacker to maintain access and potentially escalate privileges within the Xerj ecosystem, even if the initial token is revoked.

Description

Xerj is an open-source search and indexing engine tailored specifically for AI agents utilizing the Elasticsearch API, allowing AI models to query a structured index.

The vulnerability, CVE-2026-97406, stems from a flaw in how session states are authenticated and handled within the Xerj system architecture. According to the documented security contract, the issuance of new API tokens must be strictly authorized by a passkey-backed session. However, the Xerj implementation converts both standard browser sessions and API bearer tokens into the same generic AuthSession object. The token creation handler then accepts this generalized principal without verifying whether the session was authenticated via a passkey.
Because of this architectural oversight, an attacker who obtains or intercepts a valid Xerj API token can directly invoke the token creation endpoint, allowing them to create independent successor credentials with the same access levels of the original token. Furthermore, the Xerj platform lacks hierarchical revocation logic; consequently, revoking a compromised parent token has no effect on any descendant tokens spawned from it.

Impact

Exploiting this vulnerability allows an attacker to gain persistent, unauthorized access that completely bypasses multi-factor controls. The security risk escalates significantly if the compromised token belongs to a Xerj account owner. In this scenario, the newly created successor token retains full administrative authority. An attacker can use this persistent access to issue a new account invitation, redeem it in their own browser, and successfully enroll an entirely independent, attacker-controlled passkey. This grants the attacker permanent control over the Xerj instance and its sensitive data indices, rendering the revocation of the initial token completely ineffective.

Solution

The vendor could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability and an official patch has not been made available at the time of this writing. Users are advised to monitor the project's GitHub repository for updates and install the latest version of this library once a fix has been released.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to the reporter, Shiran Guez, a Principal Application Security Architect.

This document was written by Laurie Tyzenhaus.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#410595: Google BoringSSL Name Constraints Bypass in SAN Validation Logic
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Five Name Constraints findings in BoringSSL (VU#410595.8–.12) describe cases where certificate names may not be constrained as intended. Records .8, .9, .10 and .12 concern the legacy crypto/x509 path; .11 concerns the newer pki path. Two have been fixed, one is accepted, one is disputed, and one was declined.

Description

Name Constraints limit the names a subordinate certificate authority may issue. The reports concern how BoringSSL applies those limits to certain SAN (Subject Alternative Name) forms. The records do not share one status, and they do not all affect the same validation path.

VU#410595.8 (Fixed 2026-03-04): A wildcard DNS name may not be treated as covering a specifically excluded host.

VU#410595.9 (Accepted): A URI with a colon before @ may cause the wrong host to be used when matching URI constraints.

VU#410595.10 (Disputed): The finding concerns first-@ domain extraction in rfc822Name constraint matching. How consuming mail applications interpret the submitted multi-@ input, and whether that creates deployment exploitation, was not established.

VU#410595.11 (Rejected): Trailing-dot handling in rfc822Name domains. The BoringSSL team declined this on 2026-02-28 as below its security threshold.

VU#410595.12 (Fixed 2026-03-04): Trailing-dot DNS names were not always normalized on the legacy validation path.

Using BoringSSL in a product does not mean that product invokes an affected path or name form.

Impact

These findings matter only where Name Constraints are enforced on an affected path, a trusted signature can be obtained over attacker-chosen SAN fields, and the accepted name is used for authorization. Mixed-library environments may accept or reject the same certificate differently. Presence of BoringSSL does not, by itself, mean that Chrome, Android, or other products are affected.

Solution

BoringSSL fixes land in the upstream repository and reach products through each product's own update process.

  • VU#410595.8 and .12 were fixed in commit 5774eca on 2026-03-04.
  • VU#410595.9 is accepted and under coordination.
  • VU#410595.10 is disputed.
  • VU#410595.11 was declined.

CERT/CC is not coordinating BoringSSL fixes. For vendor status, contact the BoringSSL team through the Google Issue Tracker. Operators should confirm whether their deployment uses an affected path, apply available updates, and keep issued SANs well formed. A second validator helps only when it uses the same inputs and fails closed.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Oleh Konko for discovering and reporting these issues. This document was prepared with AI assistance by Timur Snoke.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#948176: Multiple TLS Libraries can Bypass Delegation Enforcement
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

This note covers thirteen library-specific records (VU#948176.6, .8–.19) of how widely used TLS libraries apply X.509 Name Constraints. The records describe cases where a constrained name may be accepted by one library and rejected by another. Some are fixed, some remain under review, and some were not accepted as security issues.

Description

Name Constraints are meant to keep a subordinate CA inside an allowed namespace. The records cover several name forms and do not all have the same classification. VU#948176.7 does not exist.

DNS case-sensitivity and wildcards. While RFC 5280 requires case-insensitive DNS matching, it does not explicitly define wildcard Subject Alternative Name (SAN) matching, leading to varied implementation behaviors. For instance, GnuTLS was found to perform case-sensitive comparisons on certain names (CVE-2026-3833, fixed in 3.8.13). Similar discrepancies regarding case handling in wildcard parent-constraint lookups were reported in Go, as well as wildcard inconsistencies in LibreSSL and wolfSSL. Additionally, pyca/cryptography was identified to check DNS Name Constraints against certificate SANs but failed to validate them against the requested peer name (CVE-2026-34073, fixed in 46.0.6).

IP addresses. Some libraries treat IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms as different when matching constraints. The Go security team determined that report did not meet its security bar; similar reports exist for Apple's Security.framework and Mozilla NSS and are included as comparative evidence.

URIs. Libraries can differ on which host they extract from a URI SAN. OpenSSL merged PR #30319 for an @ in the path, query, or fragment; a separate userinfo-colon report remains in triage. Related URI reports exist for Apple, NSS, and wolfSSL (CVE-2026-3547, fixed in 5.9.0). A well-formed single @ is handled per RFC 3986 by most implementations.

Common Name fallback. AWS-LC and s2n-tls were reported to apply DNS constraints inconsistently when a leaf has no SAN and uses a wildcard Common Name. The AWS-LC wildcard-CN issue has been fixed; a separate Unicode CN question remains under coordination. s2n-tls is in triage.

Non-critical constraints. In the reported Mbed TLS configuration, non-critical Name Constraints are not enforced. RFC 5280 requires conforming CAs to mark the extension critical, and the reviewed Mbed TLS 3.x configuration rejects unsupported critical extensions. The vendor treats adding support as a feature request; the reporter's concern remains disputed.

Impact

These records matter only when an attacker can obtain a trusted signature over chosen certificate fields, reach an affected validation path, and the application uses the accepted identity for authorization. Validator disagreement alone is not exploitation. Effects, if any, are deployment-specific and may include acceptance of a name outside the intended namespace.

Solution

CERT/CC is coordinating remediation across the affected projects. The following summarizes available status; individual entries reflect different reporting and confirmation dates.

GnuTLS — CVE-2026-3833 fixed in 3.8.13.

pyca/cryptography — CVE-2026-34073 fixed in 46.0.6.

wolfSSL — CVE-2026-3547 fixed in 5.9.0. The wildcard was addressed in PR# 9991.

Go's crypto/x509 — Two reports are in triage. The IPv4-mapped IPv6 report was not accepted as meeting the project's security bar.

OpenSSL — PR #30319 was merged and, as confirmed on 10 September 2026, is present in all then-current publicly supported versions. The separate userinfo-colon report remains in triage.

Apple's Security.framework — Three reports submitted on 2026-03-16 remain in triage.

Mozilla NSS — IP-address report under coordination.

LibreSSL — Wildcard report under coordination.

AWS-LC — Wildcard CN issue fixed; Unicode CN report under coordination. s2n-tls is in triage.

Mbed TLS — Non-critical Name Constraints are not enforced in the reported configuration. Marking the extension critical causes such chains to fail closed rather than adding enforcement.

Until updates are widely deployed, operators who depend on Name Constraints should confirm the behavior of the libraries they actually run, keep leaf certificates to explicit SANs, and treat issuance policy as the first control. A second validator helps only when it uses the same inputs and fails closed.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Oleh Konko for discovering and reporting these issues. This document was prepared with AI assistance by Timur Snoke.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#166125: Bisheng has authentication bypass vulnerabilities
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Bisheng contains three vulnerabilities: a pre-authentication account takeover mechanism via a legacy single sign-on (SSO) endpoint; an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability that exposes cross-user workflow data; and prior to version 2.5.0, authenticated attackers could perform cross-user LLM credential abuse and data disclosure due to missing service-layer access checks. Together, these flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to gain administrative control while enabling authenticated users access to sensitive data and hardcoded credentials.

Description

Bisheng is an open-source Large Language Model (LLM) application DevOps platform, developed by DataElement, designed to assist in building, managing, and scaling LLMs.

CVE-2026-96679 (Legacy SSO Bypass) A vulnerability resides in the legacy SSO endpoint (POST /user/sso). The application processes incoming JSON payloads containing arbitrary usernames and issues a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) without enforcing any form of caller authentication, such as signature verification, shared secrets, or network allowlisting. Furthermore, if the provided username does not exist, the system automatically registers the account. If this newly generated account matches the configured administrative username or is the first user in the system, it is automatically granted super-administrator privileges.

CVE-2026-96681 (IDOR Workflow Exposure) There are missing authorization controls across multiple version retrieval endpoints. The underlying source code retrieves flow and workflow version records based on user-supplied parameters without performing any data ownership or permission validation. Any authenticated user can query and read the complete Domain-Specific Language (DSL) configurations belonging to other accounts.

CVE-2026-100156 (Credential Abuse & Access Control Skip) Within the assistant service's prompt auto-optimization feature, endpoints accept an assistant identifier from the caller without verifying whether the caller owned that assistant. An assistant identifier is a mechanism that lets users or systems recognize that content or interactions come from an AI assistant rather than a human.

Impact

Authentication Bypass / Account Takeover: The legacy SSO vulnerability (CVE-2026-96679) allows unauthenticated attackers to bind their session to an existing victim's profile by completely skipping JWT validation, potentially granting full super-administrative access, leading to full application compromise.

Unauthorized Data Disclosure: The IDOR vulnerability (CVE-2026-96681) causes a breach of data confidentiality, as the system fails to properly validate whether the authenticated user has permission to access the resource.

Resource and Credential Abuse: The assistant service vulnerability (CVE-2026-100156) allows authenticated attackers to run unauthorized AI inferences billed directly to another user's provider account (such as OpenAI, Azure, or Anthropic), while also leaking the victim assistant's configured tools and workflows.

Solution

The vendor has addressed two of the three discovered vulnerabilities in subsequent software releases. CERT/CC recommends upgrading to patched releases.

CVE-2026-100156: The vendor has remediated the assistant service vulnerability in version 2.5.0.

CVE-2026-96681: The vendor has remediated the IDOR workflow vulnerability in version 3.0.0.

For the remaining unpatched vulnerability (CVE-2026-96679), DataElement/Bisheng has not responded to multiple coordination efforts. CERT/CC suggests implementing the manual mitigations below until an official update becomes available.

CVE-2026-96679 Legacy SSO Vulnerability: Administrators should consider the following defensive measures:

  • Avoid setting BISHENGPRO=true in the environment configuration.
  • Disable or deprecate the legacy SSO endpoint entirely, or enforce global JWT validation. The affected function is sso(), located in src/backend/bisheng/user/api/user.py, affecting the API endpoint POST /user/sso.
  • Restrict access to the POST /user/sso network path to loopback/same-origin to provide defense-in-depth.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Louis Sanchez, Voke Cyber, for reporting these vulnerabilities.

This vulnerability note was prepared by Laurie Tyzenhaus.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#456950: Komodo Periphery Agent Contains an OS Command Injection Vulnerability
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Versions <= 2.2.0 of Periphery, an agent within the Komodo server management platform, is vulnerable to OS command injection due to missing validation of container names, through two vectors: container destruction and container log searches. This allows an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying host, enabling persistent compromise of infrastructure.

Description

Komodo is an open-source server and deployment manager, maintained by mogh.tech, widely used in self-hosted and Docker multi-server environments. Periphery is an agent service installed on servers to give Komodo control over Docker environments.

In vulnerable versions of Komodo, Periphery does not properly validate user-supplied Docker container names before those values are interpolated into shell commands used by the agent. Two operations exhibit this vulnerability: container destruction (DestroyContainer / RemoveContainer) and container log searches (SearchContainerLog / GetContainerLogSearch). Through both avenues, raw container names are directly inserted into sh -c command lines without any shell escaping or validation. These commands then run with Periphery's root privileges on the host OS and Docker socket.

Impact

An authenticated non-admin user can escalate privileges through OS command injection via a maliciously crafted container name. Successful exploitation enables arbitrary command execution as root on a target server within a Komodo deployment. Ultimately, this enables an attacker to establish persistence, achieve lateral movement, and completely compromise a user or organization's managed infrastructure.

Solution

Fortunately, Komodo was reached to coordinate this vulnerability, and a patch has been implemented to remediate the issue in versions 2.3.0 and higher. The CERT/CC recommends that all users update immediately.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Muhammadjon Ahmadjonov for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Alex Lewis.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#382143: Lowcoder Query Library API contains cross-tenant authorization bypass allowing for data exfiltration
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Lowcoder, version 2.4.10, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its Query Library feature’s API. Authenticated users with an admin or dev role can access private library-query data from other organizations within a multi-tenant Lowcoder instance.

Description

CVE-2026-16753 Lowcoder is an open-source low-code platform that allows individuals with minimal coding experience to build web applications through a visual drag-and-drop interface. Each Lowcoder project contains a centralized Query Library which stores the workspace’s data queries and sources for quick reuse; however, the LibraryQuery API service layer lacks organization-scope checks at two endpoints: metadata retrieval and query execution.

While the application features a role-based access mechanism (requires admin or dev), it only checks the role’s validity against the user’s own organization. The vulnerable endpoints do not validate whether the requested resource belongs to the requester's organization.

Impact

Any authenticated attacker with an admin or dev role in any organization on a multi-tenant Lowcoder instance can access other tenants’ Query Libraries. Note that these roles are granted by default for any self-signup account when LOWCODER_EMAIL_SIGNUP_ENABLED and LOWCODER_CREATE_WORKSPACE_ON_SIGNUP are TRUE. This allows an attacker to do the following:

  • Read the full Domain Specific Language (DSL) of any other organization’s library queries, including complete query configuration and each referenced datasourceId.

  • Execute any library query available on the instance, receiving response data directly from the affected organization’s backend data source.

Potential impacts include cross-tenant data exposure, modification, or destruction, as well as cost abuse via querying paid data sources using another tenant’s finances. By bypassing organization-level authorization, Lowcoder instances effectively function as shared environments for attackers, violating data isolation between organizations.

This vulnerability was confirmed against Lowcoder version 2.4.10.

Solution

Unfortunately, Lowcoder could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability. To mitigate, Lowcoder administrators should restrict access to the affected Query Library API endpoints until an official security update is available. Administrators can reduce exposure by limiting application access to trusted users and reviewing admin and dev role assignments. Organizations operating multi-tenant Lowcoder deployments should consider isolating tenants into separate instances to prevent cross-organization data access. Where source-code modifications are possible, administrators should implement organization-level authorization checks for Query Library metadata retrieval and query execution.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Louis Sanchez, member of Voke Cyber, for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Alex Lewis.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#573195: Go, OpenSSL, Apple, LibreSSL, pyca, wolfSSL Name-Constraint Inconsistency in RFC 5280 Implementation
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

This note covers differences in how TLS libraries interpret X.509 Name Constraints. A certificate that one library accepts may be rejected by another. Some of those differences are defects; others follow from behavior that RFC 5280 does not fully specify.

Description

The observed differences concern DNS name comparison, IP address handling, URI-authority parsing, and wildcard matching. These include both implementation defects and behavior not fully specified by RFC 5280.

DNS-name comparison. RFC 5280 requires case-insensitive matching for DNS names. GnuTLS compared some names' case-sensitivity at the time of reporting (CVE-2026-3833, later fixed in 3.8.13). A distinct Go report concerns case handling in wildcard parent-constraint lookup, not ordinary hostname comparison.

IP address handling. RFC 5280 defines separate IPv4 and IPv6 encodings and does not say whether IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses should be treated as IPv4. Some libraries treat the two forms as different, so a constraint written for one form may not apply to the other.

URI-authority parsing. RFC 3986 allows optional userinfo before the host. Implementations differ on which host they extract when @, a colon, or a query or fragment is present. OpenSSL merged PR #30319 for an @ in the path, query, or fragment; a separate userinfo-colon report is not covered by that confirmation. Related differences have been reported in other libraries. A well-formed single @ is handled per RFC 3986 by most implementations.

Wildcard matching. RFC 5280 does not define wildcard SAN semantics. Wildcard-related reports include LibreSSL and wolfSSL. pyca/cryptography checked DNS Name Constraints against certificate SANs but not the requested peer name (CVE-2026-34073, fixed in 46.0.6), as described in the linked vendor advisory.

These differences come from independent design choices. Where the RFC is clear, some reports describe defects; where it is silent, disagreement is expected. No single library should be assumed correct for every deployment.

Impact

An attacker would need a trusted signature over chosen certificate fields, a reachable affected validation path, and an application that uses the accepted identity for authorization. Validator disagreement alone does not establish exploitation. Mixed service-mesh, CDN, or enterprise PKI environments may see different results for the same certificate. Detection is difficult because the certificate can be validly signed.

Solution

CERT/CC is coordinating with the affected projects:
* Go's crypto/x509
* Apple's Security.framework
* OpenSSL*
* LibreSSL
* pyca/cryptography
* wolfSSL

Operators who need high-assurance Name Constraints should test the validator they currently run against their deployment requirements, apply available updates, and keep leaf certificates to explicit SANs (Subject Alternative Names). A second validator helps only when it uses the same inputs and fails closed. Issuance policy and application-layer allow-lists remain useful complements where libraries differ.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Oleh Konko for discovering and reporting these issues. This document was prepared with AI assistance by Timur Snoke.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#157374: XSS vulnerability in Shopware 6 enables Admin Token Theft and RCE
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Shopware 6.7 contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its media upload functionality that can lead to administrator credential compromise and remote code execution.

Description

Shopware is an open-source e-commerce platform used to build and manage online stores. It provides merchants with customizable product pages, administrative interfaces, plugin functionality, and a media management system that allows users to upload and serve files.

CVE-2026-104937 In affected versions, Shopware’s media upload API accepts HTML files that are later served as text/html without effective Content-Security-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options security headers. An attacker with access to the media upload capability can therefore upload an HTML file with malicious embedded JavaScript, and if an administrator opens the corresponding media URL, the attacker can exfiltrate the administrator's authentication token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the Shopware Administration API.

Impact

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow an attacker with media creation/upload access to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the administrator browser context, steal valid administrator authentication tokens, and gain privileged access to the Shopware Administration API. If the affected administrator account possesses extension management privileges, an attacker could upload, install, and activate malicious plugins to achieve arbitrary PHP code execution on the underlying OS with the privileges of the Shopware process.

Solution

Shopware has confirmed that remediations are currently in development. Until a patch is available, users should follow the workaround guidance provided by Shopware linked in the "References" section below.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Deflask13 for researching and reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Molly Jaconski.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#162329: Multiple vulnerabilities in Thelia 2.6.0 and 2.6.1
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Thelia versions 2.6.0 and 2.6.1 contain multiple vulnerabilities relating to file management, Smarty templating, module installation, and administrative workflows. Successful exploitation of these issues could enable remote code execution (RCE), server-side template injection (SSTI), stored and reflected cross-site scripting (XSS), unauthorized URL redirection, and other risks that expose both server-side and client-side attack surfaces.

Description

Thelia is an open-source e-commerce platform designed to provide merchants with customizable online storefronts, product management workflows, and administrative functionalities. It utilizes the Smarty template engine and provides administrators with broad control over templates, content, and modules.

CVE-2026-103521 In Thelia v2.6.0, the document upload endpoint properly blocks the upload of executable file types, but the document update endpoint does not perform the same validation. An attacker with administrative Thelia permissions can exploit this vulnerability to upload arbitrary executable files, such as malicious PHP scripts, to achieve remote code execution on the underlying server.

CVE-2026-103522 In Thelia v2.6.0, the store banner upload feature performs insufficient filetype validation that relies exclusively on client-supplied MIME types. An attacker with administrative access can upload a PHP file disguised as an image to bypass validation and achieve remote code execution on the underlying server.

CVE-2026-103523 Thelia v2.6.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in its address creation workflow. After a user accesses a crafted URL and successfully submits the "Add New Address" form, the application redirects them to the URL specified in the next parameter. Because the application does not validate whether the destination belongs to the same origin or an approved allowlist, an attacker can supply an arbitrary external URL and redirect users to an attacker-controlled website.

CVE-2026-103524 Thelia v2.6.0 is vulnerable to multiple stored XSS vulnerabilities within the administrative interface. User-supplied input is stored without sufficient output encoding or sanitization and is later rendered in the administrator interface and/or the web store's product pages, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution when the affected pages are viewed. The vulnerability affects multiple administrative functions including category creation and product creation.

CVE-2026-103526 In Thelia v2.6.0, both the administrative login and forgotten password endpoints return different responses for invalid usernames and incorrect passwords, allowing unauthenticated attackers to enumerate valid administrator accounts. Because the endpoint also lacks rate limiting or other protections against repeated authentication attempts, username enumeration can be performed efficiently at scale.

CVE-2026-103527 Thelia v2.6.0's Smarty templates (address.html and address-update.html) fail to properly escape double quotes in the next parameter, enabling reflected XSS when an authenticated user visits the malicious link containing attacker‑controlled JavaScript.

CVE-2026-103528 Thelia 2.6.0 uses Smarty for email templates without properly restricting access to dangerous PHP functions. An authenticated administrator can inject malicious Smarty expressions into email templates via the messages configuration interface, and when the template is previewed or rendered, functions such as system(), exec(), file_put_contents(), and file_get_contents() can be executed with the privileges of the web process. This allows arbitrary OS command execution, file read/write operations, and RCE on the server.

CVE-2026-103529 Thelia v2.6.0 permits authenticated administrators to upload and install modules via the ZIP upload function without validating or sandboxing embedded PHP code. An attacker can include malicious PHP code in a module's install() method which will then be executed upon installation, enabling remote code execution with the privileges of the web server.

CVE-2026-103535 Thelia v2.6.1 contains path traversal and PHP code injection vulnerabilities in its translation editor that can be chained to achieve remote code execution. The item_name parameter, used to build the translation file's write path, does not sanitize directory traversal sequences such as ../, allowing an authenticated user with UPDATE-level permission on admin.configuration.language to write files outside templates/, including to web-accessible directories. Separately, the translation-writing logic does not escape \ in user-supplied values, allowing input to break out of the PHP string literal and inject executable code into the translation file. Chained together, these flaws allow a malicious PHP file to be written to a web-accessible path and executed with the web server's privileges.

CVE-2026-103537 Thelia v2.6.1 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability in its Smarty template handling that enables SSTI and remote code execution. The checkTemplate() validation restricts relative directory traversal sequences such as ../ but does not reject absolute paths, allowing an authorized user to supply an arbitrary filesystem path as a template. Smarty then loads and compiles the referenced file without an effective security policy, so, depending on filesystem layout and deployment configuration, template code in that file can be executed with the web server's privileges.

Impact

Several of these vulnerabilities allow authenticated administrative users to achieve arbitrary code execution on the host server. These include insufficient file validation and unsafe upload/update workflows (CVE-2026-103521 and CVE-2026-103522), unrestricted execution of PHP code during module installation (CVE-2026-103529), unsafe template evaluation for email content (CVE-2026-103528), server side template injection via absolute paths (CVE-2026-103537), and flaws in the translation writing process that permit path traversal and PHP injection (CVE-2026-103535). Exploitation of any of these issues can result in complete compromise of the underlying application environment with the privileges of the web server.

Separately, user-supplied content rendered within administrative templates enables stored and reflected XSS. CVE-2026-103524 allows persistent JavaScript execution within the admin interface, while CVE-2026-103527 enables reflected JavaScript injection via unescaped template parameters. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to hijack administrative sessions and perform privileged actions in the browser context of other authenticated users.

The discrepancies in authentication error-handling identified in CVE-2026-103526 allow unauthenticated attackers to easily enumerate valid administrative usernames, increasing the risk and effectiveness of subsequent brute-forcing or authentication-related attacks.

Finally, the open redirect described in CVE-2026-103523 allows attackers to redirect users to external attacker-controlled websites, increasing the effectiveness of phishing or other downstream attacks.

Together, these vulnerabilities facilitate full server takeover for authenticated administrative attackers, and expose avenues for browser-based compromise or credential attacks to both authenticated and unauthenticated attackers.

Solution

Unfortunately, we were unable to coordinate these vulnerabilities with Thelia, and a patch is not yet available. To reduce risk until these issues are remediated, users and organizations should restrict access to Thelia administrative interfaces, disable or tightly limit file-upload and template-editing features, and remove PHP execution permissions from user-writable directories wherever possible. Applying strict reverse-proxy controls such as rate limiting, MIME filtering, and URL allowlisting can further reduce exposure.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to the reporters K08UK0VU, s-b312, DuanNH, Deflask13, LongNBH, and NNPhong (pnn219) from ETC JSC security team for researching and reporting these vulnerabilities. This document was written by Molly Jaconski.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#553437: InsydeH2O IHISI SMM is vulnerable to unsafe memory write operations
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

An Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in the InsydeH2O IHISI software used by HP PC BIOS can allow a local attacker with OS kernel privileges to perform arbitrary physical memory writes, including writes to System Management RAM (SMRAM). Because the vulnerable code executes in System Management Mode (SMM), successful exploitation can allow an attacker to modify SMM-protected memory and potentially achieve arbitrary code execution in SMM. Depending on the platform's memory and firmware configuration, the arbitrary physical memory write primitive may also have implications for UEFI firmware update or flash-related operations.

Description

HP PC BIOS is firmware that initializes and manages hardware components during the boot process and provides runtime services to the operating system and provide the ability to update firmware. The affected system uses InsydeH2O Kernel version 5.5 or earlier. The BIOS includes custom HP SMM handlers that execute in System Management Mode (SMM), a highly privileged CPU execution mode that is isolated from the operating system.

CVE-2026-12855: An Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in the H19WMIHandlerSmm module (GUID f1946499-571b-44c3-9b9c-cc55210b0c02) allows a local attacker with OS kernel privileges to read or write arbitrary physical memory, including SMRAM, through a Software SMI handler.

An attacker with kernel-level privileges can trigger the vulnerable SMM handler by issuing a Software System Management Interrupt (SMI) through I/O port 0xB2 and supplying specially crafted CPU register values. The vulnerable handler does not adequately validate the supplied parameters before performing memory operations, allowing the attacker to influence the physical address and data involved in the operation.

Because the affected handler executes in SMM, the resulting arbitrary physical memory write can target memory regions that are normally inaccessible to software executing outside SMM, including SMRAM. Modifying SMM code or data may allow an attacker to alter subsequent SMM execution and potentially achieve arbitrary code execution in SMM. The ability to affect firmware or ROM contents is platform-dependent and is not assumed as a direct consequence of this vulnerability.

Impact

An attacker with privileged OS kernel access (ring 0) can exploit the vulnerability by raising Software SMI interrupts through I/O port 0xB2 with crafted CPU register values. Modifying SMM code or data may allow an attacker to alter subsequent SMM execution and potentially achieve arbitrary code execution and persistence via modifying SMRAM.

Solution

Users should check HP's security bulletins to determine whether their system is affected. Insyde advisory is available at https://www.insyde.com/security-pledge/sa-2026009/

Acknowledgements

Thank you to Zhenyu Liu for reporting these vulnerabilities. This document was written by Vijay Sarvepalli.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#762428: Authlib library contains a signature‑verification bypass vulnerability
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Authlib (versions up to and including 1.7.2) contain a signature‑verification bypass in the JSON Web Signature (JWS) general JSON serialization handling. The JsonWebSignature.deserialize_json() function accepts a JWS object with an empty "signatures" array and treats the payload as successfully verified, allowing attackers to supply arbitrary forged content without possessing any key material.

Description

Authlib is a Python library that provides tools for implementing OAuth, OpenID Connect, JWT/JWS/JWE (JSON Web Token / JSON Web Signature / JSON Web Encryption), and other modern authentication and authorization standards. It’s widely used in web applications and microservices to handle token creation, cryptographic validation, and secure communication.

As discussed in CVE-2026-96760, a security flaw in Authlib’s handling of JSON Web Signatures (JWS) makes it possible for an attacker to skip signature verification completely. Normally, a JWS should include at least one valid signature to prove the data hasn’t been tampered with. However, Authlib’s deserialize_json() function mistakenly accepts JWS objects even when the "signatures" section is an empty list. Because the function starts by assuming the signatures are valid and never performs any checks when the list is empty, it ends up treating unsigned data as if it were properly signed. This means an attacker could provide a JWS with no signatures, and Authlib would still treat it as trusted. Both ways of loading a JWS in Authlib are affected:

jws.deserialize_json({"payload":"...", "signatures":[]}, key=None)
jws.deserialize('{"payload":"...","signatures":[]}', key=None)

Impact

An attacker can forge arbitrary authenticated payloads without any signing key or credentials. Systems that rely on Authlib’s JWS verification for authentication, authorization, inter-service message integrity, or signed configuration data may accept attacker‑supplied content as legitimate. Potential attack scenarios inlcude the following:
* Authentication bypass: forged identity or privilege‑escalation claims (e.g., sub=admin).
* Signed message injection between microservices using JWS.
* Forged authorization claims such as scopes, roles, or permissions.
* Integrity bypass in systems relying on signed JWS data.

Solution

The vendor could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability and an official patch has not been made available at the time of this writing. Users are advised to monitor the project's GitHub repository for updates and install the latest version of this library once a fix has been released.

Acknowledgements

Thank you to Tong Hoang Gia (uziii2208) and Nguyen Minh Tuan (nguyenminhtuan28) for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Bob Kemerer.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
CERT-EU.description:
On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. Public reports indicated that these vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution (RCE).
The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities.
[New] On 23 October, PHP disclosed a new RCE vulnerability. However, it affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk. PHP will not issue an out-of-band release for this vulnerability. Instead, organisations are advised to apply mitigation to fully protect from this RCE vector.
CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
CERT-EU.description:
On 21 October 2026, GitLab published a security advisory addressing several vulnerabilities among which a critical flaw that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on a GitLab server.
CERT-EU recommends organisations to update affected assets as soon as possible, prioritising internet facing assets, and to run an assessment to identify compromised assets.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 14 October 2026, Cisco published a security advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway. This vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.
The Cisco PSIRT is aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability.
CERT-EU strongly recommends updating the Content Scanner Tools package or upgrading Cisco AsyncOS Software to a fixed release as soon as possible, prioritising appliances reachable from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking all affected appliances for indicators of compromise.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
CERT-EU.description:
On 12 October 2026, GitLab released versions 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8 of GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE), fixing 24 security issues among which a critical vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.
CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading self-managed GitLab CE/EE instances to a fixed version as soon as possible, starting with internet-facing instances.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
CERT-EU.description:
On 5 October 2026, Atlassian published a security advisory addressing a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability. It affects Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye.
CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading all affected installations to a fixed version as soon as possible, starting with instances accessible from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking access logs for signs of exploitation.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 27 September 2026, Citrix published a security bulletin addressing 8 vulnerabilities affecting customer-managed Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway, among which 2 critical unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. Citrix has confirmed active exploitation of these 2 critical vulnerabilities in the wild.
CERT-EU recommends updating affected software and running a compromise assessment on those exposed on the internet.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
CERT-EU.description:
On 22 September 2026, F5 published an advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting its BIG-IP APM product. The vendor confirmed active exploitation in the wild.
CERT-EU recommends taking appropriate actions as soon as possible.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
CERT-EU.description:
On 9 September 2026, Check Point released emergency security updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting Check Point Security Gateway, Security Management Server, and Spark Firewall deployments configured to use Remote Access VPN or Site-to-Site VPN. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS score of 9.8 and could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on affected appliances.
CERT-EU strongly recommends applying the available hotfixes as soon as possible, prioritising internet-facing and perimeter appliances.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
CERT-EU.description:
On 8 September 2026, as part of its September Security Patch Day, SAP released Security Notes addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting a broad range of SAP products[3]. The most severe, CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), is a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP Extended Passport (EPP) processing, nicknamed "OVERPASS" by the Onapsis Research Labs (ORL), which discovered and responsibly disclosed it[3]. The second, CVE-2026-58240 (CVSS 9.8), nicknamed "S4GET", is a missing authentication check in the SAP NetWeaver Message Server[6].
Both are remotely exploitable without authentication. According to the reporting researchers, successful exploitation of either can result in arbitrary operating system command execution under the account that owns the SAP installation, leading to full compromise of the affected system and the business data it holds[6].
CERT-EU strongly recommends applying SAP Security Notes 3747649 and 3759472 as soon as possible.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-010: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 19 August 2026, Citrix published a security advisory addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC (formerly Citrix ADC) and NetScaler Gateway (formerly Citrix Gateway).
CERT-EU recommends updating affected devices as soon as possible.

Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-026 - Critical vulnerabilities impacting PHP - CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 - Update 1
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Number: AL26-026
Date: October 21, 2026
Updated: October 23, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of critical vulnerabilities affecting PHPFootnote 1. In response to the vendor advisory, the Cyber centre released an advisory on October 21, 2026Footnote 2.

Tracked as CVE-2026-109618Footnote 3 and CVE-2026-109619Footnote 4, these vulnerabilities are Use After Free vulnerabilities (CWE-416)Footnote 5 affecting multiple versions of PHP. Known as “php2shell”Footnote 6, successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated threat actor to execute arbitrary code on an affected system. Internet-facing PHP servers and applications are at heightened risk.

The PHP Security Team has released security updates addressing these vulnerabilities. Organizations should identify affected systems and apply the appropriate updates immediately.

PHP remains a widely deployed technology and continues to support a substantial proportion of web applications worldwide.

All PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed are at risk. PHP assess the risk as greatest for mod_php, as a demonstrated exploit allows an unauthenticated request to trigger the vulnerability before application-level code is executed.

The Cyber Centre has observed open-source reporting indicating that a Proof of Concept (PoC) is available, with no active exploitation being identified at this time, but that can change quickly.

Update 1

On October 23, 2026, the PHP Security Team published additional information regarding another remote code execution vulnerabilityFootnote 9, tracked as CVE-2026-115560Footnote 10. The vulnerability is not addressed by the security updates released on October 21, 2026.

Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 requires an uncommon combination of PHP configuration and application behaviour. Applications that do not change the serialization handler at runtime are not exposed to this attack vector.

Until a security update is available, the PHP Security Team recommends disabling the session upload progress feature:
session.upload_progress.enabled=0

This mitigation was previously recommended for CVE-2026-109619. Organizations that have already applied this mitigation and kept it in place do not need to take additional action specifically for CVE-2026-115560.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations running affected PHP versions upgrade to the following fixed version:

affected PHP versions upgrade
Affected Product Affected Versions Fixed Versions
PHP 8.5.x prior to 8.5.12 8.5.12
PHP 8.4.x prior to 8.4.27 8.4.27
PHP 8.3.x prior to 8.3.36 8.3.36
PHP 8.2.x prior to 8.2.35 8.2.35

Note: versions 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version.

The Cyber Centre recommends that organizations:

  • Update affected PHP installations immediately to a fixed, supported release.
  • Prioritize Internet-facing systems and applications that process untrusted input.
  • Identify third-party products, appliances and containers that include vulnerable PHP componentsFootnote 7.
  • Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied.
  • Monitor for potential compromise by reviewing web server, application, authentication, and endpoint logs for suspicious activity.
  • Investigate unexpected processes, commands, files, accounts or outbound connections associated with PHP or web-server services.
  • Continuously monitor third-party vendors for security updates, including appliances, applications and services that bundle PHP, and apply applicable patches without delay.

Organizations should also review the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 8.

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-025 - Critical vulnerability impacting BeyondTrust Remote Support – CVE-2026-102764
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Number: AL26-025
Date: October 16, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of a critical vulnerability affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS)Footnote 1Footnote 2. In response to the vendor advisory released on October 15, 2026, the Cyber Centre released AV26-1054 on October 16, 2026Footnote 3.

Tracked as CVE-2026-102764Footnote 4, this vulnerability is an Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability (CWE-290)Footnote 5 that affects all versions of BeyondTrust Remote Support.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to exploit insufficient origin validation in internal BeyondTrust Remote Support messaging components to perform unauthorized file operations on an affected appliance without user interaction. The vulnerability requires no credentials or user action and can enable arbitrary file uploads, potentially resulting in full compromise of the appliance.

The Cyber Centre has observed open-source reporting indicating that the vulnerability is being exploited in the wildFootnote 6.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations running affected BeyondTrust Remote Support deployments upgrade to the following fixed version:

Affected product Affected versions Fixed versions
BeyondTrust Remote Support Versions 26.2.3 and prior BT26-05-RS patch for versions 24.3.1 to v26.2.3

BeyondTrust has confirmed that a patch addressing this vulnerability was applied to all Remote Support SaaS and Privileged Remote Access SaaS customers as of 9 October 2026. Organizations using these SaaS offerings do not need to take any additional action to remediate this issue.

The Cyber Centre also recommends organizations to:

  • identify BeyondTrust Remote Support deployments within their environments and determine whether they are SaaS-hosted or self-hosted
  • verify the installed Remote Support version. Systems running 26.2.3 or earlier are identified as affected by BeyondTrust
  • upgrade Remote Support installations older than 24.3.1 to a newer supported version before applying the remediation patch
  • apply the BT26-05-RS patch to affected self-hosted Remote Support deployments running versions 24.3.1 through 26.2.3
  • confirm automatic updates are enabled, where appropriate. BeyondTrust specifically advises manual patching for self-hosted instances that are not subscribed to automatic updates
  • as an additional defensive measure, review affected appliances for unexpected or unauthorized file activity, particularly when an appliance was exposed while vulnerable

In addition, the Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations review and implement the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 7 with an emphasis on the following topics:

  • consolidating, monitoring, and defending Internet gateways
  • patch operating systems and applications
  • harden operating systems and applications
  • isolate web-facing applications

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116104
CVE.report.description: A security flaw has been discovered in Sony Neural Network Libraries up to 1.39.0. This impacts the function func_set_nnabla_version_decorate of the file python/src/nnabla/utils/converter/utils.py of the component NNP Converter. Performing a manipulation of the argument function.type results in code injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116103
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was identified in Sony Neural Network Libraries up to 1.39.0. This affects the function load_param_in_txt of the file python/src/nnabla/utils/cli/encode_decode_param.py of the component Encode Param Command Handler. Such manipulation leads to code injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116102
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was determined in QuantGeekDev docker-mcp 0.1.0/0.2.0. The impacted element is the function _build_windows_command of the file docker_executor.py. This manipulation of the argument project_name causes os command injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116101
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was found in itsourcecode Online Cake Ordering System 1.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file /deletetransac.php. The manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116100
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability has been found in gougucms up to 4.08.18. Impacted is the function Add of the file app/admin/controller/Level.php of the component User Level Handler. The manipulation of the argument Title leads to cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115557
CVE.report.description: Python has added a denylist for known compromised certificates to the "ssl" module to ensure user safety even without certificate revocation configured. Known compromised certificates will automatically be rejected regardless of the SSLContext policy configuration.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114583
CVE.report.description:
tarfile.tar_filter could be bypassed using crafted link entries, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, to redirect later archive members outside the intended extraction directory. This allowed a malicious tar archive to cause tarfile.extractall() with filter="tar" to write files outside the destination directory, subject to the permissions of the extracting process.

This is the tarfile.tar_filter counterpart of CVE-2026-7774, which covered tarfile.data_filter.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-12345
CVE.report.description: The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory is vulnerable to a race condition. An attacker who can modify the tree during cleanup can replace a directory with a symbolic link, causing files outside of the temporary directory to be deleted or have their permissions and file flags reset, with the privileges of the process performing the cleanup. Note that platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false, remain affected, and file flags may still be reset outside of the tree on all platforms.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2024-3220
CVE.report.description:
There is a defect in the CPython standard library module “mimetypes” where on Windows the default list of known file locations are writable meaning other users can create invalid files to cause MemoryError to be raised on Python runtime startup or have file extensions be interpreted as the incorrect file type.

This defect is caused by the default locations of Linux and macOS platforms (such as “/etc/mime.types”) also being used on Windows, where they are user-writable locations (“C:\etc\mime.types”).

To work-around this issue a user can call mimetypes.init() with an empty list (“[]”) on Windows platforms to avoid using the default list of known file locations.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116099
CVE.report.description: A flaw has been found in Fusion Creators Studio SCP Containment Breach Multiplayer up to 1.295. This issue affects the function BlitzBanks of the component Skynet++ Virtual Machine. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.3R is capable of addressing this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116098
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was detected in SteelRaven7 Ravenfield 25407073. This vulnerability affects the function cacheCoverPoints of the component RFL Custom Map Handler/RFLD Custom Map Handler. Performing a manipulation results in deserialization. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The patch is named EA39 Security Patch. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116097
CVE.report.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in CloudClassroom-PHP-Project. This affects an unknown part of the file addnewstudent.php. Such manipulation of the argument fname leads to cross site scripting. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-55740
CVE.report.description: Nur-Alam39 bus-ticket (no released versions; latest commit 459cabdbeb99c00225b26e46e3c2c30ae1de7bad) contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in bus_info.php. The busid parameter received via HTTP POST is concatenated directly into a MySQL query (select * from bus_info where id=) without sanitization, escaping, or parameterization, and in a numeric (unquoted) context.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-55205
CVE.report.description: Hermes WebUI before 0.51.468 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the unauthenticated POST /api/onboarding/oauth/start endpoint that allows unbounded accumulation of in-memory flow state and daemon threads. Attackers can send repeated or concurrent requests to exhaust server memory and thread resources, potentially triggering repeated outbound device-code requests to upstream OAuth providers.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-54806
CVE.report.description: Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection in WP Activity Log <= 5.6.3.1 versions.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-54312
CVE.report.description: n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 2.24.0, an authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows could achieve global prototype pollution via the Microsoft SQL node by supplying a crafted value as the table parameter. This pollutes Object.prototype process-wide for the lifetime of the n8n server process, causing application-wide validation failures and rendering the n8n instance completely non-functional until restarted. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.24.0.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-54221
CVE.report.description:
UBB.threads is vulnerable to Reflected XSS. The application improperly handles user input in certain requests, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of a victim's browser by tricking them into clicking a crafted link. 
Because vendor contact attempts were unsuccessful, the vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 7.7.5 but may also affect other versions.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-53875
CVE.report.description: picklescan before 1.0.3 contains a scanning bypass vulnerability in the scan_pytorch function that allows attackers to embed malicious magic numbers via dynamic eval using the __reduce__ trick. Attackers can craft malicious PyTorch payloads that evade picklescan detection while remaining executable, enabling arbitrary code execution when loaded with torch.load().

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-49268
CVE.report.description:
A remote attacker can inject LDAP special characters into the Distinguished Name (DN) construction in DefaultLdapRealm class. User-supplied username input is directly concatenated into the LDAP DN template without any escaping of RFC 2253 special characters. This allows an attacker to manipulate the DN structure used for LDAP bind authentication, potentially bypassing authentication or impersonating other users.

This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 2.2.0, and 3.0.0-alpha-1 when using DefaultLdapRealm
Upgrade to Apache Shiro 2.2.1 or 3.0.0-alpha-2 or later, which fixes the issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-22674
CVE.report.description: Hashgraph Guardian through 3.6.0, fixed in commit ba8c566, contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the STANDARD_REGISTRY role to inject malicious scripts by submitting a crafted companyName value via the branding configuration API endpoint. Attackers can exploit the unsanitized innerHTML assignment in the branding service to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every authenticated user on every page load.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-7300
CVE.report.description: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability in RTI Connext Professional (Web Integration Service) allows Filter Failure through Buffer Overflow. This issue affects Connext Professional: from 7.4.0 before 7.7.0.1, from 7.0.0 before 7.3.1.3, from 6.1.2 before 6.1.*.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-8444
CVE.report.description: The WP Review Slider Pro plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'curselrevs[]' parameter of the wpfb_find_reviews AJAX action in versions up to, and including, 12.6.8. This is due to the handler reading $_POST['curselrevs'] raw with no sanitization or type casting, then concatenating each array element directly into a `WHERE id IN ( ... )` clause without quoting and executing via $wpdb->get_results() without $wpdb->prepare(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-42582

The wire encoding allows a very large length to be expressed in few bytes. There is no check that length <= in.readableBytes() before new byte[length]. This vulnerability is fixed in 4.2.13.Final.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-57881

An unauthenticated
stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in vlsvr in GeoVision
GV-LPC2011 and GV-LPC2211 V1.12 and earlier. The vulnerability is caused by
insufficient length validation when processing remote login data. A remote
attacker may exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted login data with
overly long input, resulting in memory corruption, denial of service, or potentially
arbitrary code execution.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-57880

GV-LPC2011 and GV-LPC2211 V1.12 and earlier. The vulnerability is caused by
insufficient bounds checking when parsing RTSP Digest authentication fields. A
remote attacker may exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted RTSP
request containing overly long authentication data, resulting in memory
corruption, denial of service, or potentially arbitrary code execution.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-57879
CVE.report.description:

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-57878
CVE.report.description:

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-57876
